newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Duisenberg said to favour flexibility on EMU norms.
newsitem.headline: Duisenberg said to favour flexibility on EMU norms.

text.p: Dutch central bank president Wim Duisenberg would prefer a flexible interpretation of the entry criteria for European econonomic and monetary union (EMU) rather than a delay in the January 1999 launch date, Dutch radio reported on Wednesday.

NOS radio news said Duisenberg, who is set to take over as head of the European Monetary Institute in July, had made his remarks at a closed meeting of members of parliament for Prime Minister Wim Kok's Labour Party (PvdA) two weeks ago.

It said leading Labour member of parliament Jacques Wallage had confirmed that Duisenberg discussed EMU with the party and had said at the time that the Maastricht Treaty did not insist on EMU members meeting target figures for entry exactly, as long as they had made good progress towards the targets.

In public statements, Duisenberg and other top Dutch public officials have always called for a strict interpretation of the EMU entry criteria, which include a ceiling of three percent of gross domestic product for national public sector deficits.
